final_answer: Hypothesis: There is a statistically significant difference in degree completion rates between males and females in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset. The context of this hypothesis is based on the analysis of educational attainment as measured by the highest grade completed in 1979. The variables chosen are 'Sex of respondent, 1979' (gender) and 'Highest grade completed, 1979' (degree completion rate). The analysis found that females had a slightly higher mean highest grade completed (10.61) compared to males (10.38), and this difference was statistically significant (t-statistic: -5.69, p-value: 1.29e-08).
